title: Rent the prefix: how providers sell caching
brief: You call a hosted model with a long, mostly repeated prompt. Vendors cache the prefix differently, charge differently for writes and expire entries on different clocks. The model family, request spacing and retention rules are all open.

blocks.text: What a provider cache stores, and what it charges

blocks.md: A provider cache stores the **KV tensors** for a prompt prefix, not the text. A request hits only if its prompt starts with the same tokens as a stored entry, so it saves prefill time and prefill billing but never changes the answer [[r1]]. On GPT-5.6 and later, a token is billed at exactly one of three rates: uncached, cached or cache write. Prefix order matters. Anthropic builds the prefix as `tools`, then `system`, then `messages` [[r3]].

blocks.title: Responses API request with an explicit breakpoint
blocks.caption: Illustrative shape from the 2026-10-13 docs [[r1]]. Content after the last explicit breakpoint is billed at the uncached rate with no write charge. Top-level `instructions` cannot hold a breakpoint, so put reusable instructions in a developer message.

blocks.title: Messages request with a 1-hour breakpoint
blocks.caption: Omit `ttl` for the 5-minute default. A top-level `cache_control` instead enables automatic caching, which moves the breakpoint to the last cacheable block as the conversation grows and uses one of the 4 breakpoint slots [[r3]].

blocks.title: Anthropic usage block
blocks.caption: Zero in both cache fields means the request was not cached. On Azure, Chat Completions reports `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. Track hits as cached tokens divided by prompt tokens and alert when the ratio drops.

blocks.title: Break-even for a write premium
blocks.expr: cost_cached(N) = w + r x (N - 1)   versus   cost_plain(N) = N

vars.v: write multiplier, for example 1.25 for OpenAI GPT-5.6+ and Anthropic 5-minute, 2 for Anthropic 1-hour
requests that use the prefix inside one entry lifetime

blocks.example: With w = 1.25 and r = 0.1: one request costs 1.25 versus 1, a 25% loss. Two requests cost 1.35 versus 2, already a win. Ten cost 2.15 versus 10, the example in OpenAI's guide [[r1]]. With Anthropic's 1-hour write at w = 2, two requests cost 2.1 versus 2 and three cost 2.2 versus 3. A steady stream spaced under 5 minutes refreshes the cheap entry for free, so the 1-hour TTL pays only for gaps between 5 and 60 minutes [[r3]].

blocks.title: Four ways to configure provider caching
blocks.intro: Dials: how often the prefix repeats inside the lifetime, how stable it is, the write premium, and your data retention policy.

options.name: Implicit default
options.summary: Let the provider place breakpoints. On GPT-5.6 and later it puts one at the end of the latest eligible message.
cons: Writes content that may never be reused, at 1.25x
Dynamic text early in the prompt defeats it
options.bestWhen: Append-only conversations with a stable prefix first.
options.avoidWhen: Segments change at different rates, or the tail is rarely reused.

options.name: Explicit breakpoints
options.summary: Mark where each reusable segment ends: tools, system, a reference file, history. Up to 4 cache writes per request, 3 once the implicit one is used.
pros: You choose what is written, so changing tails cost no write premium
Segments with different change rates keep separate entries
cons: Slots are limited, and Anthropic only looks back 20 block positions for an earlier write
Explicit mode with no breakpoints means no caching at all
options.bestWhen: Several segments with different change rates, or content you know is never reused.
options.avoidWhen: A simple chat, where the extra control buys nothing.

options.name: Prewarm
options.summary: Send a Responses request with `prompt_cache_options.prewarm: true` to fill the cache without generating output.
pros: The first real user request already hits
Good for startup of shared instructions and tool definitions
cons: Prewarmed tokens are billed at the write rate
Wasted if no request follows inside the lifetime
options.bestWhen: First-token latency of the first request matters.
options.avoidWhen: Low reuse, where the write is never read.

options.name: Longer retention
options.summary: Anthropic 1-hour TTL, or `24h` retention on models before GPT-5.6. On GPT-5.6 and later the only `ttl` is `30m`.
pros: Survives gaps longer than 5 to 10 minutes
Fewer repeat writes for low-traffic prefixes
cons: Extended retention stores KV on GPU-local storage, so check data retention and residency rules
options.bestWhen: Gaps between requests of 5 to 60 minutes on the same prefix.
options.avoidWhen: A steady stream under 5 minutes, which keeps the cheap entry alive for free.

blocks.title: Changed with GPT-5.6, checked 2026-10-13
blocks.md: GPT-5.6 and later added write charges, explicit breakpoints and `prompt_cache_options`, removed the 128-token rounding and deprecated `prompt_cache_retention` on Azure. The model version is dated 2026-07-09. The date the docs changed was not stated. On Azure, models before GPT-5.6 return a 400 error if sent `prompt_cache_options` or `prompt_cache_breakpoint` [[r2]]. Gemini and Bedrock follow the same idea with their own minimums and discounts, and Bedrock does not support caching with batch inference [[r4]] [[r5]].

quiz.q: On Anthropic with a 5-minute write at 1.25x and reads at 0.1x, a prefix is used by 4 requests inside one entry lifetime. What does the prefix cost, as a multiple of one uncached read of it? (Uncached, the four requests cost 4.0.)
quiz.explain: One write plus three reads: 1.25 + 0.1 x 3 = 1.55, about 39% of the 4.0 uncached cost. With a single request the same prefix would cost 1.25, a loss versus 1.0.

quiz.q: On Azure with a model before GPT-5.6, a 3,000-token prompt shows `cached_tokens: 0` on every call. The system prompt starts with the line below. Which cause fits?

code.code:
System: You are a support assistant. Current time: 2026-10-13T09:41:07Z
<2,900 tokens of fixed policy text>

options: The timestamp sits in the first 1,024 tokens, so the prefix never matches
Prompts under 4,096 tokens are never cached on Azure, whatever their content
The cache only activates after 5 requests per minute from the same user account
`cached_tokens` is only reported when `stream` is false in the request
quiz.explain: Azure needs an identical first 1,024 tokens, and one differing character gives zero cached tokens. Move the timestamp to the end of the prompt. The 4,096 figure is an Anthropic minimum for some models, not an Azure rule. There is no per-user rate gate, and streaming does not hide the field.

quiz.q: A team enables Anthropic caching but sees only cache writes and no reads. What is wrong with the request?
options: `cache_control` must sit on the first system block, never on a later block
`ephemeral` is not a valid `cache_control` type, so the request is not cached
The breakpoint sits on content that changes every request, so it only writes
System blocks cannot be cached at all, so only message content can carry a breakpoint
quiz.explain: A breakpoint on a block containing a timestamp and a user id writes a new entry every time and never matches. Put the breakpoint on the stable block, and keep the changing text after it. `ephemeral` is the valid type, position of the first block is irrelevant, and system blocks are cacheable.

takeaways: A provider cache stores KV tensors for a prefix. It changes cost and TTFT, never the answer
From GPT-5.6 and on Anthropic, writes cost 1.25x or more, so a prefix needs at least two uses to win
Static first, dynamic last. One changed character inside the cached region voids the entry
Explicit breakpoints let you choose what is written. Explicit mode with none turns caching off
Longer retention only pays for gaps between 5 and 60 minutes. A steady stream refreshes the short entry for free
